summary: This is a JUnit test class for a Thermostat that reports a status such as "Heating" or "Idle". The first test confirms a cold room turns the heat on, and the second checks that eco mode tolerates a cooler room before heating.

lines.text: Brings in the @Test annotation from JUnit 5, which is how you mark a method as a test that the test runner should execute.
A static import lets you write assertEquals(...) directly instead of Assertions.assertEquals(...), which keeps the tests short and readable.
Test classes conventionally take the name of the class under test with "Test" appended, so it is obvious that this file exercises Thermostat.
A test method name should describe the behaviour being checked, because that name is what you read in the failure report when something breaks.
Sets up the scenario: 60 degrees with eco mode off. This is the "arrange" step, where you build exactly the situation you want to inspect.
Checks the expected value against the actual one. The expected result comes first in assertEquals, and the test passes only if the two match.
The new test isolates a single rule: eco mode should shift the point at which heating begins.
66 degrees is warm enough for eco mode but would trigger heating in normal mode, so this value is chosen precisely to expose the difference between the two modes.
Asserting "Idle" here proves eco mode held off the heat; if the eco threshold were ignored, the status would read "Heating" and the test would fail.
